title: AlphaMaster: Dual-Chain Feedback for Scalable and Diverse Alpha Factor Discovery

problem.claim: Automated alpha-mining pipelines often converge to narrow expression families, causing factor homogenization, redundancy, faster decay, and limited scalability.

gap.claim: Existing automated approaches do not adequately maintain diverse alpha discovery while preserving predictive strength and scalability.

contributions.claim: AlphaMaster formulates alpha mining as a closed loop of hypothesis generation, experimental evaluation, and feedback-guided refinement.

AlphaMaster combines reinforcement learning, Generative Flow Network sampling, large language model-based symbolic synthesis, and genetic programming in a dual-chain generation-and-optimization design.
By accounting for correlations in its diversity constraints, the framework reduces redundant signals while strengthening predictive performance and stability.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Under realistic trading constraints on CSI 500 and CSI 1000 data from 2010–2025, the authors report that AlphaMaster ranks first on five of six CSI 500 metrics and all CSI 1000 metrics.
The authors report CSI 500 IC of 0.050, AR of 0.136, and IR of 1.464.
The authors report CSI 1000 IC of 0.069, RankIC of 0.091, AR of 0.150, and IR of 1.410.

narrative_sequence.summary: Alpha mining seeks predictive and interpretable cross-sectional return signals, but automated pipelines can produce homogenized and redundant factors.
AlphaMaster frames alpha mining as a feedback loop connecting hypothesis generation, evaluation, and refinement.
The framework uses a dual chain that separates diverse proposal generation from multi-objective optimization and integrates several discovery techniques.
Correlation-aware diversity is used to reduce redundancy while supporting predictive strength and stability.
Experiments on CSI 500 and CSI 1000 under realistic trading constraints are reported to show strong multi-metric performance.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines proposal generation with feedback-guided, multi-objective refinement and explicitly controls correlation-aware diversity.

interpretation.claim: Discovery systems may benefit from separating exploration of diverse candidates from later optimization under explicit redundancy constraints.

application.claim: Apply a two-stage discovery workflow in settings where candidate homogenization reduces coverage or long-term usefulness.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this design generalizes beyond alpha-factor discovery or the reported market datasets.

unknowns: Comparative baselines and their exact evaluation results are not specified.
Statistical significance, ablation results, and implementation details are not provided.
The abstract does not define the six evaluation metrics in full.
